problem: Recent VLN models are very large (~190M params) and computationally heavy, which risks overfitting and hinders deployment on edge robots. Existing KD methods target single-stage classification and use one-step, one-way teacher-to-student transfer.
motivation: VLN combines single-modal encoding, cross-modal fusion, topological memory and sequential decisions, so it is unclear what to distill and how. Teachers are also fallible, and a large capacity gap makes direct distillation to tiny students hard.
key_idea: Decouple a VLN agent into five meta-abilities and distill each with randomized and uncertainty-aware loss weighting, then chain teacher-student pairs of decreasing size with interactive co-training so students also improve teachers.
insight: Distilling all five meta-abilities together works best, and removing the global topological ability (G) hurts most (SR 73.95 vs 76.33). Removing all KD drops SPL from 67.86 to 64.82. Teacher-uncertainty weighting matters: beta=0 costs 1.6% SPL and beta=0.9 costs 4.5%. Interactive co-training improves the teacher too, and continuing to train the teacher without student feedback overfits, so the gain comes from mutual exchange rather than extra training.
method: MAKD: splits the agent into five meta-abilities (visual perception, textual interpretation, local panoramic cross-modal matching, global topological cross-modal location, behavioral decision) and transfers meta-knowledge at each module's last layer, using attention and feature MSE for transformer modules and temperature KL on logits for the decision head.
Student scaling: shrinks hidden size and layers (B 384-d, M 256-d, S 128-d) to give 57.88M, 30.23M and 11.14M params, versus the 190.96M teacher (GOAT).

MKRW: samples random Gaussian weights for the M meta-knowledge losses at each iteration, normalizes them with a scaled softmax (K=5, tau=4), and thereby adds gradient noise to escape sharp minima, with no learnable parameters.
MKTD: computes teacher uncertainty as cross-entropy against the ground-truth action and weights each sample's distillation loss by exp(-beta*U), with beta=0.7.
ICoD S1-S2: trains the teacher normally, then trains a smaller student from scratch with MAKD+MKRW+MKTD while the teacher provides step-wise guidance on the student's own actions.
ICoD S3-S4: co-trains teacher and student with mutual distillation at a lower learning rate (5e-6, up to 20K iterations), then uses the refined student as the next teacher for a smaller model.

setting.backbone: GOAT/DUET-style dual-scale graph transformer (RoBERTa text encoder, CLIP ViT-B/16 image features), trained from scratch as students of sizes L/B/M/S
setting.training_data: R2R (with PREVALENT augmentation and speaker back-translation) and RxR-English (with Marky-mT5-MP3D augmentation), original MP3D scenes only, no ScaleVLN extra scenes; VLN@TJ for sim-to-real fine-tuning (110 paths)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views, CLIP features), no depth or semantics
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints, with a stop token
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (plus a self-collected real-robot dataset, VLN@TJ)

numbers.extra: original MP3D data only; ICoD co-trained

numbers.eval_set_note: 2 unseen scenes, 26 paths, 93 instructions (computed from the reported dataset split)
numbers.extra: R2R checkpoint fine-tuned on VLN@TJ; FPS on an i7-4600U CPU
numbers.evidence: Table sim-to-real, Comparison on the test set of VLN@TJ

numbers_note: Ablation results for MKRW, MKTD beta and feature types are given only in figures. The 93-instruction count for VLN@TJ is derived, not printed.
results: With only MP3D data, MAGIC-L reaches R2R test-unseen SR 77.02 / SPL 68.73, beating the teacher GOAT (74.57 / 64.94) and roughly matching ScaleVLN (77 / 68), which uses 1,291 extra scenes. MAGIC-S, with 11M params and 2 GFLOPs, reaches SR 75.17 / SPL 65.13 on test-unseen, above GOAT. On the real-robot dataset it also beats GOAT in SPL (54.66 vs 48.04) at 14.75 FPS versus 1.02.
limitations: Failure on instructions with only directional actions and no semantic landmarks
Students still lag the teacher on RxR val-seen, and the largest R2R val-seen gap appears for the smallest model
Real-world dataset is tiny (5 scenes, 26 test paths), so ICoD was not applied there; ICoD gains rely on the teacher being retrained jointly
